title: Sum of All Matrix Elements
description:
A 2D array stores values in rows and columns. Visit every element with two nested loops and add them up.

Input: The first line has `r` and `c`, followed by `r` lines with `c` integers each.
Output: One integer, the sum of all elements.

title: Largest Element in a Matrix
description:
Start with the first element as the largest so far, then compare it with every other element.

Input: The first line has `r` and `c`, followed by `r` lines with `c` integers each.
Output: One integer, the largest element.

title: Row Sums
description:
Add the elements of each row separately. Reset the running sum at the start of every row.

Input: The first line has `r` and `c`, followed by `r` lines with `c` integers each.
Output: `r` lines, line `i` holds the sum of row `i`.

title: Column Sums
description:
Add the elements of each column separately. The outer loop should go over columns.

Input: The first line has `r` and `c`, followed by `r` lines with `c` integers each.
Output: One line with `c` integers separated by single spaces; the j-th value is the sum of column `j`.

title: Main Diagonal Sum
description:
In a square matrix the main diagonal holds the elements `a[0][0]`, `a[1][1]`, ... where row index equals column index.

Input: The first line has `n`, followed by `n` lines with `n` integers each.
Output: One integer, the sum of the main diagonal.

title: Anti-Diagonal Sum
description:
The anti-diagonal runs from the top-right to the bottom-left corner. Element `a[i][j]` is on it when `i + j == n - 1`.

Input: The first line has `n`, followed by `n` lines with `n` integers each.
Output: One integer, the sum of the anti-diagonal.

title: Add Two Matrices
description:
Add two matrices of the same size by adding the elements in the same position.

Input: The first line has `r` and `c`. Then come `r` lines for matrix A, then `r` lines for matrix B, each with `c` integers.
Output: The resulting matrix, one row per line, values separated by single spaces.

title: Transpose of a Matrix
description:
The transpose swaps rows and columns: element `a[i][j]` becomes element `[j][i]` of a matrix with `c` rows and `r` columns.

Input: The first line has `r` and `c`, followed by `r` lines with `c` integers each.
Output: The transposed matrix with `c` lines, each holding `r` integers separated by single spaces.

title: Search an Element in a Matrix
description:
Check every element and see whether it equals the target value.

Input: The first line has `r` and `c`, followed by `r` lines with `c` integers each. The last line has the target integer `x`.
Output: Print `Found` if `x` appears in the matrix, otherwise `Not Found`.

title: Sum Above the Main Diagonal
description:
In a square matrix, the elements above the main diagonal are those where the column index is greater than the row index (`j > i`).

Input: The first line has `n`, followed by `n` lines with `n` integers each.
Output: One integer, the sum of all elements strictly above the main diagonal.

title: Symmetric Matrix
description:
A square matrix is symmetric if it equals its own transpose, i.e. `a[i][j] == a[j][i]` for all `i` and `j`.

Input: The first line has `n`, followed by `n` lines with `n` integers each.
Output: Print `Symmetric` or `Not Symmetric`.

title: Identity Matrix
description:
An identity matrix is square, has 1 on the main diagonal and 0 everywhere else.

Input: The first line has `n`, followed by `n` lines with `n` integers each.
Output: Print `Identity` or `Not Identity`.

title: Multiply Two Matrices
description:
To multiply A (`r1 x c1`) by B (`c1 x c2`), each result element `[i][j]` is the sum of `A[i][k] * B[k][j]` over all `k`.

Input: The first line has `r1 c1 c2`. Then come `r1` lines for A (each with `c1` integers) and `c1` lines for B (each with `c2` integers).
Output: The `r1 x c2` product matrix, one row per line, values separated by single spaces.

title: Rotate Matrix 90 Degrees Clockwise
description:
Rotating clockwise turns the first column (read bottom to top) into the first row. The result has `c` rows and `r` columns. Hint: new[j][r-1-i] = old[i][j].

Input: The first line has `r` and `c`, followed by `r` lines with `c` integers each.
Output: The rotated matrix, one row per line, values separated by single spaces.

title: Sum of Boundary Elements
description:
Boundary elements lie in the first row, last row, first column or last column. Make sure no element is counted twice (corners belong to two edges, and a 1-row or 1-column matrix is entirely boundary).

Input: The first line has `r` and `c`, followed by `r` lines with `c` integers each.
Output: One integer, the sum of boundary elements.

title: Row with the Maximum Sum
description:
Compute the sum of every row and find which row has the largest sum. If several rows tie, choose the smallest index. Rows are numbered from 0.

Input: The first line has `r` and `c`, followed by `r` lines with `c` integers each.
Output: Two integers on one line: the row index and its sum, separated by a space.

title: Saddle Point
description:
A saddle point is an element that is the smallest in its row and also the largest in its column. Scan rows from top to bottom, left to right, and report the first saddle point.

Input: The first line has `r` and `c`, followed by `r` lines with `c` integers each.
Output: The value of the first saddle point, or `None` if there is no saddle point.

title: Spiral Order Traversal
description:
Print the elements in spiral order: left to right along the top row, down the right column, right to left along the bottom row, up the left column, then repeat inside the remaining layer. Hint: keep four boundaries (top, bottom, left, right) and shrink them after each side.

Input: The first line has `r` and `c`, followed by `r` lines with `c` integers each.
Output: One line with all `r*c` elements in spiral order, separated by single spaces.

title: Generate a Spiral Matrix
description:
Fill an `n x n` matrix with the numbers 1 to `n*n` in spiral order: start at the top-left corner, go right, then down, then left, then up, turning whenever you hit the edge or a filled cell, and keep spiralling inward.

Input: One integer `n`.
Output: The matrix, one row per line, values separated by single spaces.

title: Determinant of a Square Matrix
description:
The determinant of a 1x1 matrix is its only element. For a larger matrix, expand along the first row: the sum over columns `j` of `(-1)^j * a[0][j] * det(minor)`, where the minor is the matrix without row 0 and column `j`. A recursive function works well.

Input: The first line has `n`, followed by `n` lines with `n` integers each.
Output: One integer, the determinant.
